html:
Terpenes are natural aromatic compounds found in cannabis (and many fruits, herbs, and flowers). They’re responsible for the smell, flavor, and subtle effects of different strains, why one strain smells citrusy while another is earthy or piney.

Beyond aroma, terpenes work alongside cannabinoids to shape the overall experience.

Why Terpenes Matter

Terpenes help influence:

  • How a strain smells and tastes

  • Whether effects feel uplifting, calming, or balanced

  • The overall character of the experience

They play a key role in the entourage effect, enhancing how cannabinoids like THC and CBD feel.

Common Cannabis Terpenes

Myrcene

  • Aroma: Earthy, musky, herbal

  • Commonly linked with relaxing, body-focused effects

Limonene

  • Aroma: Citrus, lemon, orange

  • Often associated with uplifting, bright effects

Pinene

  • Aroma: Pine, fresh forest

  • Frequently linked to alertness and clarity

Linalool

  • Aroma: Floral, lavender

  • Commonly associated with calming and soothing effects

Caryophyllene

  • Aroma: Spicy, peppery

  • Known for a grounding, balanced feel

Terpenes + Cannabinoids = The Entourage Effect

Terpenes don’t work alone. When combined with cannabinoids, they create a more well-rounded and nuanced experience than any single compound on its own.

That’s why two strains with similar THC levels can feel completely different.

How to Read a Terpene Profile

When viewing a product’s terpene profile, look for:

  • Dominant terpenes (top 2–3 listed)

  • Aroma descriptions that match your preference

  • Balanced profiles rather than just high THC

Choosing by terpenes often leads to better results than choosing by strain name alone.
